samples.identification: WorkspaceAgent/1.0: custom native x64 remote-management agent; family unassigned
samples.reason: On balance, an evasive preconfigured remote agent with server-directed watchdog recovery is likely hostile in this corpus. This is a contextual judgement; remote administration and watchdogs individually remain dual-use.
evidence: Unsigned C++ PE. Native TLS callback at VA 0x7ff7c1390000 probes CPUID leaf 1 hypervisor bit and vendor leaf 0x40000000, PEB NtGlobalFlag+0xbc mask 0x70, virtual hardware registry/device artifacts and usernames. Some gates lead to termination.
TLS routines decode XOR wide strings and manually resolve PE exports with FNV64 offset basis 0xcbf29ce484222325 and multiplier 0x100000001b3.

Main application has WebRTC/libdatachannel transport, CORE_CONTROL dispatch and server-layout policy handling. Traced policy code handles autorun service/task settings, recovery configuration and re-arms watchdog tiers from the server layout.

Stack-built manifest endpoints are https://georgejiy339-creator.github.io/Hello/runtime/manifest.js and https://panel.diablo-net.top/runtime/manifest.js. Forager attempts returned HTTP 404 and DNS failure respectively; no remote content recovered.

AES-GCM-related TLS descriptor processing is present. The mapped code regions examined are plaintext; eight attempted offline GCM decryptions failed authentication. Successful decryption is not claimed.
samples.missing_context: No installation authorization, operator identity, runtime session or functioning manifest response. No basis to assign the many unrelated families in the collector filename or to claim credential theft.
samples.coverage_gap: Original now has three suspicious findings but zero hostile findings. A hostile rule cannot be justified by promoting CPUID/debug checks, API hashing or remote administration alone. The watchdog-plus-hypervisor combination is suspicious co-occurrence, not proof of a malicious command. Decoded stack/XOR configuration and recovery paths were investigated; generic endpoint patterns would overclaim C2 and exact endpoint strings would be specimen-specific.
samples.marker: WorkspaceAgent: evasive remote agent with watchdog re-arming

samples.identification: IconLib 0.73 managed icon library carrying an appended AutoIt RunPE stage
samples.reason: The ordinary icon library is a carrier: an executable AutoIt container is concealed after SignedData inside an inflated certificate table. Its recovered script hollows explorer.exe and patches native process APIs, behavior unrelated to icon manipulation.
evidence: Managed .NET 2.0 IconLib 0.73 code and the embedded EmptyDll template implement ordinary icon-library operations. The managed DLL entry was not found to invoke the appended AutoIt script.
Authenticode digest and signature remain intact: Expressco Services LLC, DigiCert code-signing chain, signed 2025-06-05. This does not authenticate bytes following the DER SignedData object.

Certificate table begins at file offset 69632, declared size 4213544. The aligned SignedData end is 80168. An EA06 archive starts at 81962 within approximately 4.2 MB of unsigned certificate-table trailing data.
AutoIt decompression exceeds the ripper default 10 MB ceiling; raising it to 30 MB recovers a 6528719-byte deassembled script and a 3009536-byte x64 native PE from initial hex assignments.

Recovered script line 3098 calls CreateProcessW with CREATE_SUSPENDED=4 and explorer.exe selected as the host. It obtains thread context, parses/maps the supplied PE, uses VirtualAllocEx RWX, unmaps the original image, writes replacement headers/sections and image base, sets thread context, and resumes the thread.

On Windows 24H2 the script writes bytes 48 31 C0 C3 (xor rax,rax; ret) to ZwManageHotPatch and a second ntdll location derived from RtlEqualUnicodeString+784 or a module-relative fallback before ResumeThread.
The extracted native payload uses additional obfuscation, manual API/syscall wrappers and analysis checks; no final family, credential source or exfiltration endpoint is asserted.
samples.missing_context: Companion AutoIt interpreter and deployment command are missing. The appended script is an independently recoverable executable archive, but loading this managed DLL alone is not shown to execute it. The signer is not attributed as the author of the appended malware.
samples.coverage_gap: Original has one hostile certificate-padding rule. Scanner does not automatically decompress this EA06 container, so recovered hollowing and native patch findings require extraction. Two suspicious source observations plus one hostile combination now cover that extracted script. Original hostile count remains below the 3-5 goal; adding raw-byte hollowing claims would misrepresent the compressed bytes. Ultimate obfuscated native-stage behavior remains unresolved.
samples.marker: IconLib carrier: unsigned AutoIt payload hollows explorer.exe

extracted_script_comparison.note: Manual extraction; not an automatically reported archive member.

samples.identification: Obfuscated Go PE memory loader containing a Remus-matching native payload
samples.reason: An executable-image loader concealed by layered transforms and hundreds of generated junk blocks manually maps a native payload and substitutes process identity structures. The recovered payload also matches the Remus family signature; the loader behavior independently supports the judgement.
evidence: Go 1.23.1, CobaltVectorStudios source path, randomized identifiers and approximately 607 repetitive junk blocks. Intact self-signed Cobalt Vector Studios certificate supplies no independent publisher trust.

main.arJGDJ at VA 0x593160 reconstructs a 336567-byte buffer. Decoding subtracts 31*i+14, reverses the buffer, subtracts 13*i+123, swaps adjacent pairs, then subtracts 7*i+47, modulo 256, recovering an x64 PE.

Main loader parses MZ/PE headers and sections. main.lZ20DmaI resolves and calls VirtualAlloc with MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE=0x3000 and PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE=0x40. Subsequent code copies image headers/sections and resolves imports/relocations before invoking the mapped entry point via syscall.SyscallN.
main.nR0Q8 obtains the TEB through NtQueryInformationThread. main.faCOJRTI at VA 0x519340 follows TEB+0x60 to PEB and stores mapped base at PEB+0x10.
main.fzsVS1ElNi follows PEB+0x20 to ProcessParameters and replaces ImagePathName and CommandLine UNICODE_STRING data. Other helpers update loader/activation-context state.

Extracted payload matches third_party/CAPE/Remus. Native GDI, COM/WMI and user/computer API capability evidence exists, but this review does not infer a particular credential collection or exfiltration flow from imports or the family name.
samples.missing_context: No successful live execution, operator infrastructure, credential source or exfiltration target recovered. Family signature corroborates, rather than establishes, the behavioral verdict.
samples.coverage_gap: Original now has two distinct hostile combinations: arithmetic PE unpacking/manual mapping and packed PE image-base substitution. A third hostile outcome is not invented. Additional process-parameter rewriting is manually traced; generated junk separates the relevant pointer sources and sinks by large gaps, and the existing bounded instruction matchers do not robustly prove that data flow. Payload behavior beyond the loader remains partly obfuscated.
samples.marker: Remus loader: decodes PE, maps it, and replaces PEB image base

trait_changes: Extended existing Go byte-transform, RWX allocation ABI and entry-base setup matchers without removing old alternatives. Existing hostile combinations now fire on the obfuscated Go loader.

Extended canonical NtGlobalFlag check to x64, renamed x86-peb-ntglobalflag-mask-branch to peb-ntglobalflag-mask-check, preserved all four x86 branch variants and updated the sole live fixture expectation. Exact and ancestor consumers reviewed; no live rule consumer required changes.
Added executable-section-bounded hypervisor-vendor probe and FNV64 PE-export walk, a neutral watchdog diagnostic and a suspicious watchdog/hypervisor combination.

Added structural EA06 container-after-SignedData observation and hostile intact-CA-signature plus unsigned certificate-padding composite. No filename, signer identity, exact size or endpoint is required.

Added recovered AutoIt source observations for suspended process replacement and native zero-return patching, with a hostile composite requiring both. Source rules do not assert these names occur uncompressed in the DLL.
preservation: All original findings, including the embedded PE member in IconLib.dll, remain. No original matcher was weakened or removed. The new FNV64 and CPUID matchers were restricted to executable sections after data-decoy checks; original sample coverage was retained.

regressions.stage_extraction: extract_stages.py independently reproduced both native payloads and the AutoIt source; hashes recorded in scratch/bad-analysis/reproduced/extraction.json

classifier_disagreement: All three original ML outputs remain cls=0, lvl=-1 despite behavioral MALICIOUS judgements. Probabilities increase for the remote agent and Go loader; the carrier aggregate stays dominated by its embedded template. Extracted AutoIt rises from 0.03220433 to 0.9235495 but also remains lvl=-1. Feature-spec v18 versus current expected v21 was reported by atomscan, so a model/feature update is a separate remaining gap. No inaccurate or duplicate rule was added to force a classifier label.
runtime_limit: Static reverse engineering only; samples were never executed. Failed remote retrieval and failed offline GCM authentication are explicitly not treated as successful behaviors.
